By 2031, AI-assisted case analysis and accommodation planning will plausibly speed the seminar component of this practicum, and observed-usage data shows AI concentrated in exactly that kind of writing and analytic support work. The supervised classroom placement itself -- managing real children with disabilities across diverse assessment and instructional situations -- is not something a model performs; it is embodied, real-time, and interpersonal. Verification burden stays high because misjudged accommodations or behavioral responses affect actual students, keeping a trained supervisor's oversight necessary. The practicum's role as a required clinical gateway to student teaching does not loosen within a five-year catalog cycle. The instrumental case for the practicum itself is preserved; the seminar's supporting materials are what shift, and the rating holds Low.

Over a decade, considerably more capable AI systems (consistent with the METR task-horizon trend) may reshape how candidates prepare for and reflect on practicum placements, generating richer case analyses or simulated scenarios for seminar discussion. Whether that meaningfully reduces the instrumental need for the supervised placement itself is uncertain and depends on regulatory choices about clinical-hour requirements that are not visible from current trends; macro-level estimates of AI's economy-wide productivity effect over a decade remain modest, suggesting institutional practice will not transform as fast as raw capability. The practicum's function as the required bridge to student teaching, verified through direct supervision of work with real children, is the more durable feature. The rating holds Low, with substantial uncertainty concentrated in program design rather than task automatability.
SED 4440.d: This practicum is a culminating experience that provides teacher candidates with a structured, supervised elementary and/or secondary level practicum in a special education setting for children with disabilities. A strong emphasis is placed on the importance of decision-making in diverse contexts, including numerous assessment and instructional situations using a case-based approach that will encourage integration of theory and application. The seminars are designed to address assigned topics and activities that are linked to the teaching responsibilities of the practicum.

r: This is full-time, full-responsibility student teaching: a candidate is assigned an actual group of learners with exceptionalities in an accredited school for a minimum eight-week block, with university supervisors conducting observations and guiding a teacher work sample. The activity is Training and Teaching Others and Guiding, Directing, and Motivating Subordinates performed continuously, in person, with legal responsibility for real students' instruction and safety -- the most presence-dependent, lowest-exposure category task-exposure research identifies. The binding constraint is absolute: enrollment requires completion of all special education licensure program requirements, and the experience itself is the Colorado-board-mandated clinical capstone that certifies readiness to teach. At 24 months, no plausible AI deployment substitutes for a candidate holding full instructional responsibility for a classroom of students with disabilities.

AI lesson-planning and IEP-documentation assistance will likely be routine in K-12 special education classrooms by 2031, and jagged-frontier findings caution that overreliance outside a system's competence can leave less-experienced teachers worse off, not better, if trust is miscalibrated -- a real risk for a novice managing a full caseload of students with exceptionalities. None of that substitutes for the embodied, real-time work of running a classroom, adapting instruction moment to moment, and being legally and professionally accountable for named students under an assigned cooperating teacher. Verification burden is at its structural maximum here since the candidate herself is the accountable party under supervision. The licensure-capstone requirement does not loosen on a five-year catalog cycle. The rating remains Low, anchored by embodiment, accountability, and the licensure mandate together.

Projecting a decade out, AI classroom tools will be considerably more capable and diffused, but student teaching's function is certifying a candidate's own competence to independently manage instruction for students with exceptionalities under live supervision -- a credentialing act, not merely a task bundle, and the course is terminal within the program rather than a prerequisite substrate. There is no confident basis for predicting that Colorado licensure boards will replace supervised full-time teaching with an AI-mediated alternative by 2036; diffusion research shows institutional adoption consistently lagging raw capability. The honest uncertainty is about what tools student teachers use during the placement, not about whether the embodied, supervised capstone itself remains required. The rating holds Low, with high confidence given the depth of the licensure and presence constraints.
SED 4490.d: This course is a full-time, special education, student teaching experience in an accredited, public or private school that provides teacher candidates responsibility for teaching an identified group of learners with exceptionalities. A minimum of eight weeks is required for 6 credits, and a minimum of 16 weeks is required for 12 credits. University supervisors provide regularly scheduled observations and seminars, as well as guidance on the development of the teacher work sample.
